packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: fresh Claude subagents (Opus 5.5), image-only, one per packet; packets 01 and 06 sent back to the same reader for further passes on named tiles; the packet-01 reader consulted an advisor model on process only (no readings), as its response states; local file paths written by the reader were reduced to file names before publication (28 November 2026), no other change
text:
packet-18 - unverified blind image reading
Reader: isolated first reader. No identification or prior reading was in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md, the image files, and crops I made of them (crops stored in the scratchpad, paths given below). packet.json was not read (it was only seen as a filename in a directory listing of the packet folder).

LAYOUT SURVEY (written after viewing image-001; other images surveyed as they are opened)

image-001 (1291x1800, whole leaf, one face, with colour bar below): a single leaf mounted in a paper/guard frame, upright. Two zones:
- Left half: diagrams, no prose. Top: a grid of 9 columns x 9 rows of numerals (each row repeats one numeral across: from bottom row upward 1, 2(?), 3, 4(?), 5, 6, 7, 8, 9), with a row of small arched cells above carrying numerals with small superscript marks, and a fan of intersecting semicircular arcs over the whole grid (looks like an abacus / place-value table). Below: a rectangle lettered f, m(?), h at top and e, o, c(?) at bottom with a vertical line from m to o, two circles (one above, one below the rectangle's mid-line), the word "columpna" under the bottom edge, and "tu ...... bus"(?) written across the middle line. Faint drypoint/plummet circles and lines also visible behind. A small red mark at lower left.
- Right half: one column of prose, about 27 lines, in a small gothic textualis bookhand, brown ink. Paragraph marks (capitulum signs) inside the lines. Interlinear superscript numerals or letters (small arabic-type numerals/letters such as 1, 2, 3, 4... written above certain words) appear over many lines: tentatively a numbering of definitions. A two-line block at the top of the column is separated from the main column by a space and is in the same hand (end of a preceding section?). A marginal mark "p"(?) to the left of the line beginning "igure" (the initial F seems not written: "[F]igure" with space left for an initial; tentative). Show-through from the other face is visible across the column.
- Observation: text is mathematical definitions (numbers, places, digits, articles, differences). Interpretation only, no identification attempted.

CONVENTIONS: line numbers are text lines of the right-hand prose column of image-001, counted from the top of that column (L1 = first written line at y~300 px). Superscript (interlinear) numerals/letters are given as ^[...] at the point where they stand. Medieval numeral forms: in L3 the sequence is written with older forms (2 looks like "7", 4 like a looped "ℓ", 5 like a modern "4", 7 like "Λ"); I give modern values with the visible shape in brackets where useful. Crops: c001_0.png (L1-L9), c001_1.png, c001_2.png (same folder), all 2x enlargements of the column.

TRANSCRIPTION, image-001, right column (read from image-001 and crop c001_0)

image-001 L1: g^o(ergo?) vid[e?]t(ur)(?) calefi(t)(?) et(?) centrum ignis ascendit(?) q(?) i(n) eis s(u)p(r)a po(n)it[..](?)   [first glyph g with superscript o; "et" is an odd ligature, could be "ex"; last word "pōit-" with a stroke, ending unclear]
image-001 L2: attendetur.
   [gap of about one line; then the main section begins]
image-001 L3: [F](?)igure numeroru(m) sunt . 1 . 2[7-shape] . 3 . 4[looped] . 5[4-shape] . 6 . 7[Λ] . 8 . 9 . (et)(?) est   [no initial painted: the line begins "igure" with a blank before it; a small marginal mark like "p" or "F" to the left, at the column edge - possibly a guide letter for the initial]
image-001 L4: p(ri)ma unitatis . s(e)c(un)da binarii (et) sic deinceps. ¶ Or^[1]
image-001 L5: do locorum figurarum a p(ri)mo loco incipit in
image-001 L6: finitum p(ro)cedens et a dext(ra)(?) incipiens t(er)minu(m)   [the superscript over "dext" could also be a numeral; uncertain]
image-001 L7: non accipit a sinist(ra). ¶ ^[3](?)Omnia loca p(ri)mo (et)(?) eode(m) su   [symbol between "primo" and "eodem" is a ꝯ/&-like sign, uncertain: (et) or q(uam)?]
image-001 L8: mu(n)t(ur). Omnia a p(ri)mo equidistantia p(ro)(?) eodem. ¶ ^[looped mark, 4?]Nu(merus)(?)   [last word written "Nūc"/"Nu" with a stroke; read Nu(merus) from the next line]
image-001 L9: simplex est qui una sola rep(re)sentat(ur) figura. ¶ ^[.4.-shape = 5?]Digi
   (L10-L17 read from crop c001_1)
image-001 L10: tus est nu(meru)s a quo figura denominat(ur) sive q(ui)c(um)(?)   [last word "q̄cū" with marks, uncertain]
image-001 L11: p(ri)mo loco una sola rep(re)sentat(ur) figura · ¶ ^[.6.]Com
image-001 L12: posit(us) nu(meru)s est q(uem)(?) diu(er)se rep(re)sentant figure u(e)l una
image-001 L13: plies sumpta. ¶ ^[.Λ. = 7]Suplemen(tum)(?) loci est ci[f/ſ]ula(?) uel c(ir)cu(?)   [word after "est" ambiguous: "cifula"/"cisula"/"sciſula"; "ciu" with stroke at line end]
image-001 L14: la est signum loci uacui a figura. ¶ ^[8]Nu(meri) simplices
image-001 L15: a loco primo equidistantes d(icu)nt(ur) nu(meri) eiusde(m) differe(n)c(ie).   [brown hook-like mark in left margin at this line]
image-001 L16: ¶ ^[9, written like ꝯ](?)Nu(meri) p(ri)me d(iffe)r(enti)e s(un)t(?) q(ui)(?) d(iffe)r(un)t(?) differencia unitatum ab u   ["cue" and "df" with strokes: uncertain]
image-001 L17: nitate s(ecundu)m(?) un(ius)(?) addicio(n)em ordine naturali p(ro)cedu(n)t
   (L18-L25 read from crop c001_2)
image-001 L18: usq(ue) ad denarium. ¶ ^[.10.]Omnis figura per se considerata   [a small mark like ".!" or a hyphen-sign stands after the word, at the column edge]
image-001 L19: aliq(uem)(?) simplicium nu(mer)or(um) p(ri)me d(iffere)(n)c(i)e representat. ¶ ^[.11.]O(mn)is
image-001 L20: d(iffere)n(ti)a .9. continet nu(mer)os s(ecundu)m q(uan)titatem p(ri)mi ipsor(um)
image-001 L21: ge(?) t(ra)nsgredientes. ¶ ^[.12.]Omnis d(iffere)n(ti)e nu(meru)s p(ri)mus tociens [sign](?)   [first word "ge" as written, unexplained; final sign at line end is a t-like letter with a small superscript, unread]
image-001 L22: coac(er)uet(ur)(?) ut ex singulis coac(er)uat(i)o(n)ibus(?) singuli   [both words written "coacu-" with superscript marks; a green stain covers part of the second, but the letters remain visible]
image-001 L23: reliquor(um) eiusdem d(iffere)n(ti)e nu(mer)or(um) (et) p(ri)mus sequentis d(iffere)n(ti)e
image-001 L24: fiunt. ¶ ^[13] [qm̄/Nu?](?) similes sunt quos eadem figura rep   [the word after ¶ is a q- or N-like letter with abbreviation bar, not the same shape as "Nu" in L8/L14/L16; uncertain]
image-001 L25: sentat. ¶ ^[14?]Equidistantes nu(meri) sunt int(er) [ēqs: q(uo)s? eos?](?) [ginue / p(ri)me?](?)   [last two words uncertain; text continues on another face]

image-001 left half, diagram labels (read from image-001 directly):
- Grid: 9 x 9 cells; each row a single numeral repeated 9 times; rows from top: 9, 8, 7[Λ], 6, 5[4-shape], 4[looped], 3, 2[7-shape], 1. Above the top row, a row of arched cells with numerals and superscript marks (shapes like 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 each with a small superscript stroke/letter, reading right-to-left?); not legible in detail at this scale.
- Lower figure: letters f (top left), m (top middle), h (top right), e (bottom left), o (bottom middle), c or 6 (bottom right); "tu ........ bus"(?) across the middle; "columpna" below the bottom line.
- Unread on this face: nothing in the prose column is left unread; small superscripts in the arched cells of the grid not resolved.

image-002 (1151x1904): native-resolution detail of the numeral grid on the left half of the image-001 face (same object as the grid in image-001; not additional text). No prose. Observations:
- Bottom 8 rectangular rows, 9 cells each, numerals repeated across, bottom to top: 1; 2 [7-shape]; 3; 4 [looped, like a cursive ℓ/ꝗ]; 5 [modern-4 shape]; 6 [σ-like]; 7 [Λ]; 8.
- Top row: 9 small semicircular-topped cells each containing 9.
- Above that, under the large arcs, one numeral per column with a small superscript sign (a short stroke over a small "a"/"α"-like loop) above each: left to right 9, 8, 7[Λ], 6, 5[4-shape], 4[looped], 3, 2[7-shape], 1. So the series runs 9 down to 1 from left to right.
- Nine large semicircular arcs of increasing span spring from the top of the grid, all ending at the right edge (the leftmost begins at the left edge); they overlap like a fan.
- Faint plummet/drypoint circle and lines behind (not ink).
- No words visible on this tile.

image-003 (1151x1905): native-resolution detail of the lower left half of the image-001 face (overlaps image-002 by the bottom row of 1s). No prose. Observations:
- Ink rectangle with corner letters: top left "f", top middle "m", top right "h"; bottom left "e", bottom middle "o", bottom right "c" (or "6"/"σ"-shaped). A vertical line joins m to o.
- Two ink circles: one whose lower arc reaches the middle of the rectangle and whose upper part rises above the top edge f-m-h; a second below, rising from the middle and extending below the bottom edge e-o-c. The circles touch near the middle of the vertical line.
- Across the middle, between the two circles: "cu" + a long wavy connecting stroke + "bus" (i.e. "cu~~~~bus" as written; I read the first letters as "cu", earlier on image-001 I wrote "tu" - "cu" is the better reading at this resolution).
- Under the bottom edge, below "o": "columpna".
- Faint grey plummet/drypoint construction drawings behind (a circle at upper right, intersecting straight lines and arcs at left, possibly with small letters); not ink, not read.
- A red mark at lower left, like "f." or "1." in red; meaning unclear.

image-004 (1728x1772): native-resolution tile of the TOP of the prose column of the image-001 face. It shows L1-L14 of the column (image-004 line n = column line Ln as numbered above; the same lines as image-001, not additional text). Bottom edge of image-004 is L14 ("la est signum loci uacui a figura. ¶ Nu(meri) simplices"). Also crop c004_a.png (L1-L2 and L6-L8 enlarged).
Revised/confirmed readings at this resolution (where different from the image-001 reading, the image-004 reading is the better one):
image-004 L1: g^o(ergo?) vid[u/i]s'(?) calef[ia]t with stroke (calefi(un)t? calefa(ci)t?) ēē(esse?) centrum ignis ascendit^(ur?) q̄r(?) ī(in) eis stupa pōita(posita)   [I now read the odd word after "calef-" as "ēē" (esse?) not "et/ex"; the word before "pōita" reads "stupa" letter by letter (s-t-u-p-a), not "s(u)p(r)a"; "pōita" with o and stroke]
image-004 L2: a[cc/tt]endetur.   [2nd-3rd letters could be "cc" or "tt"; c/t are close in this hand; I cannot settle from the letterforms alone]
image-004 L3: [F](?)igure numeror(um) sunt . 1 . 2[7-shape] . 3 . 4[looped] . 5[4-shape] . 6 . 7[Λ] . 8 . 9 . (et)(?) est   [sign before "est" is a "τ"-shaped (et) sign; no zero/cipher figure is written in the list; small mark "p"/"F" in the left margin]
image-004 L4: p(ri)ma unitatis . s(e)c(un)da binarii (et) sic deinceps. ¶ ^[1]Or
image-004 L5: do locorum figurarum a p(ri)mo loco incipit in
image-004 L6: finitum p(ro)cedens et a dext(ra) incipiens t(er)minum   [superscript over "dext" is the same "ra"-type sign as over "sinist" in L7, so not a numeral]
image-004 L7: non accipit a sinist(ra). ¶ ^[.3.](?)Omnia loca p(ri)mo [ꝯ/&-like sign] eode(m) su   [the superscript over "Omnia" looks like a 3 (ʒ-shape) with points either side; no superscript "2" seen anywhere in L4-L7]
image-004 L8: mu(n)t(ur). Omnia a p(ri)mo equidistantia p(er)/p(ro)(?) eodem. ¶ ^[.looped 4.]Nu(merus)(?)   [the superscript is the looped shape used for 4 in the grid]
image-004 L9: simplex est qui una sola rep(re)sentat(ur) figura. ¶ ^[.4-shape. = 5]Digi
image-004 L10: tus est nu(meru)s a quo figura denominatur siue q̄c(um)(?)
image-004 L11: p(ri)mo loco una sola rep(re)sentatur figura · ¶ ^[.6.]Com
image-004 L12: posit(us) nu(meru)s est q(uem)(?) diu(er)se rep(re)sentant figure u(e)l una
image-004 L13: plies sumpta. ¶ ^[.Λ.=7]Suplemen(tum)(?) loci est [ciſula/cifula](?) uel ci(r)cu(?)
image-004 L14: la est signum loci uacui a figura. ¶ ^[8]Nu(meri) simplices
Note: the superscript numerals form a sequence 1 (Ordo), 3 (Omnia loca), 4 (Numerus simplex), 5 (Digitus), 6 (Compositus), 7 (Supplementum), 8 (Numeri simplices...), 9 (Numeri prime differentie), 10, 11, 12, 13, 14(?). Observation only: no "2" is visible; either it is not written or one of my numeral readings is off by one.

image-005 (1728x1773): native-resolution tile of the LOWER part of the prose column of the image-001 face. It shows L12-L25 (image-005 line 1 = L12, line 14 = L25). Overlap with image-004: L12-L14 (same lines, not additional text). Bottom of image-005 is the last written line of the column (L25).
Readings at this resolution (image-005 line / column line):
image-005 1 (L12): posit(us) nu(meru)s est q(uem)(?) diu(er)se rep(re)sentant figure u(e)l una
image-005 2 (L13): plies sumpta. ¶ ^[.Λ.=7]Suplemen(tum)(?) loci est [s]ci[ſ/f]ula(?) uel ci[ſ/f]u   [at this size the line-end word looks like "ciſu"/"cifu" rather than "c(ir)cu"; both words are uncertain at letter level]
image-005 3 (L14): la est signum loci uacui a figura. ¶ ^[8]Nu(meri) simplices
image-005 4 (L15): a loco primo equidistantes d(icu)nt(ur) nu(meri) eiusde(m) differe(n)cie.
image-005 5 (L16): ¶ ^[.9.]Nu(meri) p(ri)me d(iffere)n(ti)e [cue/sue with stroke](?) [df with stroke](?) differencia unitatum ab u
image-005 6 (L17): nitate s(ecundu)m(?) un(ius)(?) addicio(n)em ordine naturali p(ro)cedu(n)t
image-005 7 (L18): usq(ue) ad denarium. ¶ ^[.10.]Omnis figura per se considerata :-   [":-"-like mark at line end, outside the column]
image-005 8 (L19): aliq(uem)(?) simplicium nu(mer)or(um) p(ri)me d(iffere)n(ti)e representat. ¶ ^[.11.]O(mn)is
image-005 9 (L20): d(iffere)n(ti)a .9. continet nu(mer)os s(ecundu)m q(uan)titatem p(ri)mi ipsor(um)
image-005 10 (L21): se t(ra)nsgredientes. ¶ ^[.12.]Omnis d(iffere)n(ti)e nu(meru)s p(ri)mus tociens [t-like sign with stroke](?)   [correction to my image-001 reading "ge": the first letter is the same round/g-like s that begins "simplex" (L9) and "similes" (L24), so "se"]
image-005 11 (L22): coac(er)uet(ur)(?) ut ex singulis coac(er)uat(i)o(n)ibus(?) singuli   [green stain over the middle of "coac-"; letters still visible]
image-005 12 (L23): reliquor(um) eiusdem d(iffere)n(ti)e nu(mer)or(um) (et) p(ri)mus sequentis d(iffere)n(ti)e
image-005 13 (L24): fiunt. ¶ ^[13][q/c with stroke, m or ui](?) similes sunt quos eadem figura rep
image-005 14 (L25): sentat. ¶ ^[.14.?]Equidistantes nu(meri) sunt int(er) [ēos/q̄s](?) s[..]ue(?)   [superscript is "1" plus a looped digit = 14?; last word begins with the same round s, middle minims unclear]

AREAS SELECTED AND UNREAD
- Selected and read: the whole prose column of the one face present (L1-L25), at both overview and native resolution; diagram labels.
- Not read / unresolved: the small superscript signs over the numerals in the arched row of the grid (image-002); the faint plummet drawings and any letters in them (image-003); show-through text from the other face (visible in reverse across the column, not attempted). Only one face of the leaf is in this packet; the text continues beyond L25 (ends mid-sentence) and begins before L1 (L1 starts mid-sentence), so adjacent leaves/the verso would be needed.

LIMITATIONS
- Unverified image reading. Expansions are proposals. Words most in doubt: L1 (vid?s, calef-, ēē, q̄r), L2 (accendetur/attendetur), L7 sign between "primo" and "eodem", L10 last word, L13 "sciſula"/"ciſu-la", L16 "cue df", L21 final sign, L24 first word after ¶, L25 last two words.
- Superscript definition numbers: 1, 3-14 seen; no 2 found.
- Exposure: nothing in my context revealed an identification or a prior reading. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules except make enlarged crops (permitted); I saw the filename packet.json in a directory listing but did not open it.
- Image limit not reached; all five images opened.

LATE RE-LOOK (written with composite crop c_relook.png in view; enlarged pieces of image-004 and image-005)
- L4 superscript over "Or": a slanted stroke with a small curl at the top. Closer to the plain "1" of L3 than to the 7-shaped 2 (no horizontal top bar), but not certain. The "no 2 found" note stands, with this caveat.
- L1 words 2-3: word 2 begins with an r- or v-like letter; "r/v-i-d-u-s" or "r-e-d-u-s", still unresolved. Word 3 reads "calefi" + "a" with a stroke + "t" (calefia(n)t?) rather than "calefi(un)t". I did not re-check "ēē".
- L2: the 2nd and 3rd letters stick up slightly above the x-height, like the t in "-detur". So on letterforms alone "attendetur" is slightly favoured over "accendetur". Still uncertain.
- L7 sign between "primo" and "eodem": a bulky æ/ꝗ-like sign. It is not the same as the p(er)/p(ro) sign before "eodem" in L8 (p with a stroke through the descender), nor the p(ro) of "p(ro)cedens" in L6. Unresolved; (et) withdrawn as a proposal, leave as [sign].
- L25 last two words: the word after "int(er)" is e + a round letter (o or round d) + s with a stroke, so "ēos"(?) rather than "q̄s". The last word begins with a 9-shaped sign (con-) with a straight descender, not the round s, followed by "[a/ti]nue". So: "ꝯ[ti/a]nue" = (con)tinue(?).
- L21 line-end sign: my crop missed it (wrong region). Not re-checked.

FILE CORRECTIONS
- The layout survey said "about 27 lines". The column has 25 written lines (L1-L2 plus L3-L25).
- Where the image-004/image-005 readings and the late re-look differ from the image-001 readings, the later ones supersede the earlier ones for L1-L25.
- Beyond the rules, also disclosed: I ran an ls glob on the responses directory for existing packet-18 files (no matches) and created the responses directory with mkdir -p (it already existed or was created; no other files were read). Image count: 5 images + 5 crops = 10. Image limit not reached.
